Nth Nota Privacy Policy

Effective October 19, 2026. Nth Nota is provided by Brad Redenbach, An Nth Experience. Privacy and support contact: annthexperience@gmail.com.

Your notes and recordings

Notes, tasks, drawings, imported files, original voice recordings, transcripts, note history, settings and assistant conversations are saved in the app’s storage on your device. Nth Nota does not require an account and does not automatically sync your desk to our servers. Uninstalling the app or clearing its storage can remove this data. Use Backup & restore to keep a copy.

Permissions you choose

Microphone access is used for voice notes when you start recording. Notification access is used for reminders and optional task notifications you choose. Notifications may display task text; Android lock-screen and channel settings control visibility and delivery. File import and export use the system file picker. Granting permission does not start recording, turn on cloud processing or create reminders. You may decline permissions, revisit them in Settings, or revoke them in Android app settings.

Local AI, handwriting, speech and readback

On supported devices, Android’s AICore and ML Kit process writing requests and speech locally. Model preparation may download files and contact Google services. Availability varies by device, language and installed system components. Original audio files are not uploaded by the transcription feature. Readback in the Android app uses an installed offline voice. A browser’s speech engine may have different data practices.

Handwrite to text uses Google ML Kit Digital Ink Recognition on this device. Your pen and finger strokes and recognized words are not sent to Google by the recognizer. The first conversion in a language downloads a language pack (about 20 MB); after it is downloaded, conversion can work offline. Stopping closes the conversion request, but a language-pack download already started may finish in the background. Google ML Kit receives SDK diagnostics and usage metrics, including device and app information, installation identifiers, performance, feature events, errors and configured languages. See ML Kit privacy terms and ML Kit data disclosures.

Optional cloud AI

Local writing AI is tried first. Before cloud fallback is used, you must allow it in the app. After that choice, fallback can happen automatically when local AI is unavailable. The app sends your request, selected text or current note context, and recent conversation turns over HTTPS to our Cloudflare Worker. The Worker uses Cloudflare Workers AI or configured Groq to produce a reply. Other notes, original audio files, image files and the rest of your desk are not included by this feature. Text you include in a request or note context is included, so remove private information you do not want processed in the cloud.

Our writing endpoint does not write prompts or replies to its D1 quota database. It records daily usage counters keyed by a salted daily hash derived from the connection IP address, and provider cooldown information, to enforce free limits and reduce abuse. This hash is pseudonymous rather than a guarantee of anonymity. Cloudflare necessarily receives network connection information. Operational logs and provider data handling are separate from the app’s quota storage.

Cloudflare’s standard Workers AI inference policy describes transient content processing, no model training on customer content, operational metadata, and limited legal/security exceptions. Groq’s inference policy describes no default input/output retention, with reliability or abuse-monitoring exceptions of up to 30 days unless a longer period is legally required; account data controls may further limit retention. We do not claim those account controls have been enabled. Read the current policies: Cloudflare Workers AI and GroqCloud. Their terms and policies govern their processing. Requests may be processed outside your country.

Cloud AI is optional and limited. Turning it off prevents new cloud writing requests; it does not retract requests already processed. Core notes remain usable when AI is unavailable or an allowance is exhausted.

Reporting an AI reply

If you explicitly submit a report, the edited reply excerpt, reason, optional details, a random report ID and submission time are sent through Cloudflare to the developer’s report database for reviewing safety and improving the app. The report form does not automatically include your original note or other chat messages. Failed reports stay on this device and are not retried automatically. Sent reports are retained for 30 days, then removed at the next daily scheduled cleanup. Contact us about deleting a submitted report and provide its report ID. Removing a local report does not remove a report already received by the developer.

Retention, deletion and backups

Your local desk remains until you delete it or clear app storage. Recently deleted items remain recoverable until you permanently delete them. Settings → Privacy & data lets you delete the local desk, including saved reports and conversations. This also clears scheduled app task notices and turns cloud AI off; Android permission grants are managed separately. Exported backups are readable files containing notes and attachments. Store them privately and delete them separately when no longer needed. Imported backups do not grant Android permissions or restore cloud consent.

Quota records older than two days and reports older than 30 days are removed by the gateway’s daily scheduled cleanup. Network and provider metadata may follow separate retention policies. Contact the privacy address above with questions or deletion requests. Nth Nota has no advertising SDK, sells no user data, and does not add an advertising or separate analytics SDK. Google ML Kit’s SDK diagnostics are described above.

Security and changes

The Android app restricts its embedded browser to bundled app files and uses HTTPS for cloud requests. Provider API secrets are held on the gateway, not in the APK. Device security and exported backup security still depend on how you protect your phone and files. We will update this policy when data practices change and request a new choice before a materially different cloud use.
